_comment: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; r5-only family (no r4 predecessor). Pairs with RA (RA-3(1) supply-chain risk assessment is the trigger for the SR program), SA (SA-4 acquisition clauses are the contract vehicle for SR program requirements; SA-9 external-services governance overlaps with SR-3 / SR-5; SA-15(3) criticality echoes SR-3), and CM (SR-10 inspection of components feeds CM-2 baseline integrity). The SR family formalizes what was scattered across r4 — the practitioner shorthand: 'r4 had SCRM bolted into SA + SI + RA; r5 extracted it into its own family.'
title: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan
description: Documents how supply-chain risk is identified, assessed, and mitigated across the system's lifecycle. Covers SCRM plan governance, processes for managing supply-chain risk, acquisition strategies that select trustworthy suppliers, supplier assessments and reviews, notification agreements, inspection of received components, anti-counterfeit / authenticity controls, and component disposal. Covers the controls of the SR family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-161 r1 (Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices), NIST SP 800-53A r5 (Assessment), Executive Order 14028, OMB M-22-18 / M-23-16 (software supply chain), Section 889 of the FY2019 NDAA (covered telecommunications), CISA ICT-SCRM Task Force guidance, and FedRAMP Continuous Monitoring requirements.
intro_template:
This Supply Chain Risk Management Plan documents the SCRM approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, criteria, cadences, and roles used to maintain a SCRM Plan, govern supply-chain risk processes, develop acquisition strategies that select trustworthy suppliers, assess supplier risk, establish notification agreements, inspect received components, protect against counterfeit components, and manage component disposal across the supply chain.

The scope covers SCRM plan governance per SR-2, supply-chain processes / controls per SR-3, acquisition strategies per SR-5, supplier assessments per SR-6, notification agreements per SR-8, component inspection per SR-10, authenticity (anti-counterfeit) per SR-11, and component disposal per SR-12 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Supply Chain Risk Management family), NIST SP 800-161 r1 (Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices), and EO 14028 / OMB M-22-18 software-supply-chain guidance.
approach_template:
{system_name} SCRM is governed by {scrm_team_role} who maintains the SCRM Plan at {scrm_plan_location}. Vendor risk is assessed through {vendor_risk_management_system}, with assessments performed on the cadence in §4.5. Acquisition strategies select trustworthy suppliers per the criteria in §4.4, with contractual notification obligations per §4.6. Components are inspected upon receipt per §4.7, with anti-counterfeit controls per §4.8 and disposal per §4.9.

Additional details on SCRM plan governance, processes and controls, acquisition strategies, supplier assessments, notification agreements, inspection, authenticity, and component disposal are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Supply-chain-risk performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (SCRM Plan currency, supplier-assessment completion rate, vendor-incident notification timeliness, counterfeit-component detections, SBOM-completeness rate, single-source-component count, Section 889 / 889A attestation currency, vendor-EOL anticipation lead time). Vendor-incident notifications received are processed against the IR plan workflow within the SLA negotiated in SR-8 agreements. SBOMs received from suppliers are matched against vulnerability data on the cadence required by RA-5 / SI-2.
integration_template: This Supply Chain Risk Management Plan does not stand alone. The RA family supplies RA-3(1) supply-chain risk assessment that triggers SR program activity; the SA family supplies SA-4 acquisition clauses that contractually impose SR requirements, SA-9 external-services governance overlapping SR-3 / SR-5, and SA-15(3) criticality echoing SR-3; the CM family receives SR-10 inspection results into CM-2 baseline integrity; the IR family processes vendor-incident notifications received per SR-8; the SI family verifies authenticity of artifacts produced by suppliers per SI-7. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where SR-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Roles and tooling that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: SCRM-team role (one-liner)
questions.help: Role / team accountable for SCRM (e.g., 'Agency C-SCRM Office', 'Internal SCRM Working Group chaired by CISO + Procurement Lead', 'ISSO with quarterly review by ITRM committee').

questions.label: SCRM Plan location
questions.help: Where the SCRM Plan itself is maintained (typically alongside the SSP — e.g., 'eMASS package PKG-12345 SCRM annex', '/repo/compliance/scrm-plan.md').

questions.label: Vendor risk-management system (one-liner)
questions.help: Where vendor-risk-rating is conducted (e.g., 'Internal review + BitSight + SecurityScorecard', 'Archer Vendor Risk module', 'CISO-led annual vendor review with Procurement support').

questions.label: SBOM processing tooling
questions.help: Tool that ingests and analyzes received SBOMs (e.g., 'OWASP Dependency-Track', 'Anchore Enterprise', 'Mend SCA + custom ingestion').

questions.label: Methodology alignment
options: NIST SP 800-161 r1 partial — major-vendor scope only
NIST SP 800-161 r1 partial — software-supply-chain only

family_questions.label: SCRM Plan (SR-2)
family_questions.description: How the SCRM Plan itself is governed.

questions.label: SCRM Plan scope summary
questions.help: What the SCRM Plan covers (organizational responsibilities, in-scope suppliers / categories, risk methodology cross-reference to RA-3(1), incident protocols, plan revision schedule). Reference NIST SP 800-161 r1 Appendix B.

questions.label: Plan-review cadence (SR-2 ODV)
questions.help: How often the SCRM Plan is reviewed and updated (typical: 'Annually + on significant change to supplier mix or threat environment'). SR-2 ODV.

questions.label: Dedicated SCRM processes (SR-2(1))
questions.help: Per SR-2(1) — establish a dedicated supply-chain risk-management team. Document team membership, charter, decision authority.

family_questions.label: Supply Chain Controls and Processes (SR-3)
family_questions.description: Risk-mitigation processes applied across the supply chain.

questions.label: Risk categories addressed
options: Quality / defect risk from supplier process

questions.label: Mitigation strategies
options: Source diversification (multiple suppliers per critical category)

questions.label: Evaluation methodology
questions.help: How candidate suppliers are evaluated. Scoring matrix, weight per criterion, decision authority. Reference NIST SP 800-161 r1 Appendix C.

questions.label: Trusted-supplier list reference
questions.help: Where the approved-supplier / trusted-supplier list is maintained.

questions.label: Source-diversity requirement
questions.help: When source-diversity (multiple suppliers per critical component class) is required vs allowed-single-source. Risk-acceptance pathway for unavoidable single-source dependencies.

questions.label: Assessment inputs
options: Third-party risk-rating service (BitSight / SecurityScorecard / Black Kite)

questions.label: Assessment cadence (SR-6 ODV)
questions.help: How often suppliers are reassessed. Tier-based (e.g., 'Critical suppliers: continuous + quarterly formal; high-risk: semi-annual; standard: annual').

questions.label: Adverse-finding handling
questions.help: Workflow when a supplier assessment identifies elevated risk. Acceptable-risk pathway, mitigation requirements, exit / replacement consideration.

questions.label: Critical-supplier register
questions.help: Who is on the critical-supplier register and why. Reference RA-9 criticality analysis.

questions.label: Required notifications
options: Cybersecurity incidents affecting customer data / systems
Government investigations / subpoenas affecting customer data

questions.label: Notification SLA
questions.help: Time-to-notify by event class. Common: 'Cyber incidents: 24-72h per CISA / DFARS guidelines'; 'Vulnerabilities: per coordinated disclosure timeline'.

questions.label: Contract clause reference
questions.help: Pointer to the standard contract-clause language that imposes notification obligations.

questions.label: Internal-routing of received notifications
questions.help: Where notifications received from suppliers are routed internally (typically: SOC + ISSO + IR team). Reference IR plan.

questions.label: Inspection triggers
options: Indicator of compromise published for component class

questions.label: Inspection methods
options: X-ray / non-destructive testing for embedded modifications

questions.label: Failure-handling procedure
questions.help: What happens when inspection reveals a problem. Component quarantine, supplier escalation, IR activation. Coordination with CISA-DHS.

questions.label: Anti-counterfeit training program (SR-11(1))
questions.help: Per SR-11(1) — training for personnel involved in receipt / inspection / disposal of components. Reference AT-3 role-based training.

questions.label: Genuine-source verification (SR-11(2))
questions.help: Per SR-11(2) — verifying components are obtained from authorized suppliers / authorized resellers. Maintaining the chain back to the OEM.

questions.label: Suspected-counterfeit register reference
questions.help: Where suspected-counterfeit findings are recorded and tracked.

questions.label: Disposal procedures
questions.help: How disposal is executed. Coordination with MP-6 sanitization (for media-bearing components), PE-16 removal, vendor RMA workflow with required sanitization. Reference NIST SP 800-88 r1.

questions.label: Chain-of-custody requirement
questions.help: Whether and when chain-of-custody documentation is required for disposal. Especially relevant for cryptographic-module-bearing components and classified-system components.

family_questions.label: Supply-Chain Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: Active suppliers
questions.help: Approximate count of active suppliers in scope of SR program.

questions.label: Critical suppliers
questions.help: Approximate count of suppliers classified as critical (per SR-3 / RA-9).

questions.label: Open-source dependencies tracked
questions.help: Approximate count of OSS components tracked through SBOM analysis.

questions.label: Quarterly components received
questions.help: Approximate count of components received per quarter (anchors SR-10 inspection effort).

family_questions.label: SCRM Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate SR control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: Supplier-assessment completion rate (% of in-scope suppliers reassessed in cycle)
Vendor-incident notification timeliness (mean time received vs SLA)
SBOM-receipt completeness rate (% of contracts with SBOM delivered)
Vendor-EOL anticipation lead time (mean days notice received)
Trusted-supplier list currency (% reviewed in cycle)
Open POA&M items linked to SR controls

questions.label: Triage role
questions.help: Who triages received vendor notifications (typically SOC dispatcher or IR analyst-on-call).

questions.label: IR-handoff workflow
questions.help: How vendor-incident notifications become incidents in the IR plan workflow. Severity determination, escalation criteria.

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the SR control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.16').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for SR findings
questions.help: Convention for SR-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-SR-' for general).

questions.label: RA handoff
questions.help: How RA-3(1) supply-chain risk assessment triggers SR program activity. How RA-9 criticality classification feeds SR-3 critical-supplier register.

questions.label: SA handoff
questions.help: How SA-4 acquisition clauses contractually impose SR requirements; SA-9 external-services governance overlap with SR-3 / SR-5; SA-15(3) criticality echo with SR-3.

questions.label: CM handoff
questions.help: How SR-10 inspection results feed CM-2 baseline integrity. Component-tampering finding triggers CM-4 / CM-5 review.

questions.label: IR handoff
questions.help: How vendor-incident notifications become IR-plan events. How counterfeit-component detection escalates.

questions.label: SI handoff
questions.help: How SR-supplied artifact authenticity (SBOM, signed packages, attestations) feeds SI-7 integrity verification.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying SR continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management — practice covering the full set of activities to manage cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain. Per NIST SP 800-161 r1.
Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States — federal interagency committee reviewing foreign investments in US businesses for national-security concerns.
Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act — 2022 US law requiring critical-infrastructure entities to report cyber incidents to CISA. Drives SR-8 vendor-notification clauses.
Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification — DoD's framework assessing contractor cybersecurity posture. Often required as SR-5 pre-award criterion.
A component falsely represented as genuine (e.g., re-marked silicon, fake serial numbers, knock-off PCBs). SR-11 controls protect against.
Electronic Resellers Association International — industry organization providing counterfeit / non-conforming component reporting.
Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence — disclosure required of suppliers in US national-security acquisitions.
Government-Industry Data Exchange Program — federal information-sharing program for product-quality and counterfeit-component issues.
Information and Communications Technology Supply Chain Risk Management Task Force — CISA-administered public-private partnership developing SCRM practices.
Framework for software-supply-chain integrity, providing cryptographic attestations for each step of the build process. Used in SR-10 inspection of digital deliverables.
Original Equipment Manufacturer — the producer of a component as opposed to a reseller. SR-11(2) genuine-source verification traces back to the OEM.
Return Merchandise Authorization — a vendor process for returning failed components. Subject to SR-12 / MP-6 sanitization requirements before return.
Software Bill of Materials — formal record of components in software. Required by SR / SA-4(10) per EO 14028 / OMB M-22-18.
Per SR-2, a documented plan describing how supply-chain risk management is performed. Reference NIST SP 800-161 r1 Appendix B.
Section 889 of the FY2019 NDAA — prohibition on US government use of certain Chinese telecom and surveillance equipment (Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua, Hytera). Drives SR-5 pre-award attestation.
Risk arising from dependence on one supplier for a critical component. Mitigated by source diversification per SR-3.
Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts — a security framework specifying levels of supply-chain integrity guarantees. SLSA Level 3+ provides build-pipeline protection.
Unauthorized modification of a component. Per SR-10 / SR-11, inspection on receipt detects tampering; tamper-evident packaging surfaces it.
A supplier that has been vetted and approved per the organization's SCRM criteria. Maintained on the trusted-supplier list referenced by SR-5.
